name: Exchange password spray
behaviour: EBurst-style password spraying across Exchange interfaces
data_sources: Exchange IIS W3C logs: c_ip, cs_username, cs_uri_stem, sc_status (all ten Exchange virtual directories)
false_positives: Load balancers, reverse proxies or NAT egress presenting many users as one address; Mobile gateways after a password-policy change
positive_test: Replay of the lab spray (64 mailboxes, 104 failures, 4 interfaces from 203.0.113.47) fires once
negative_test: Monday-morning logon surge and the mobile gateway's routine failures stay silent
response: Score only. Check the source's reputation; if it is internal, open a host investigation. Watch AA26-D02 for a success.

name: Spray source authenticated
behaviour: A sprayed account then authenticates from the spraying source
data_sources: Exchange IIS W3C logs: c_ip, cs_username, sc_status
false_positives: A user who mistyped once behind the same NAT as a spray (rare; check the user agent)
positive_test: j.citizen: failed once from 203.0.113.47 during the spray, then 200s from the same address: fires once
negative_test: Users who succeed from the gateway during a spray without first failing from it stay silent
response: Treat the account as compromised: reset the password, revoke sessions and tokens, confirm MFA on every Exchange protocol, and review mailbox activity since the success.

name: Scanning on advisory ports
data_sources: Firewall or NetFlow: src, dest, dest_port
false_positives: Approved vulnerability scanners and monitoring; Internet background scanning
positive_test: 203.0.113.47 (41 hosts, 6 ports) fires; so does the internet background scanner, at low score
negative_test: The internal vulnerability scanner 10.20.0.50 is excluded by the lookup
response: Score only. Internal source scanning: open a host investigation.

name: Web enumeration burst
data_sources: Web server or WAF logs: src, uri_path, status, http_user_agent
false_positives: Authorised web application scans and penetration tests
positive_test: 203.0.113.47's 450 missing script paths in ten minutes fire once
negative_test: Normal 404s from broken links stay silent
response: Score only. Correlate with exploitation attempts against the same server.

name: Exploit attempts for advisory CVEs
behaviour: One source trying several of the advisory's exploited CVEs (2014-2023) and XSS payloads against web servers
data_sources: Web server, reverse proxy or WAF logs: c_ip, cs_method, cs_uri_stem, cs_uri_query, cs_User_Agent, sc_status
false_positives: Authorised vulnerability scanners and penetration tests; Security research crawlers
positive_test: 203.0.113.47: 7 techniques (six advisory CVEs plus XSS), 15 requests, 2 answered: fires once
negative_test: The approved scanner 10.20.0.50 (4 techniques) and a one-technique background probe stay silent
response: Score the source. Check which requests were answered (status below 400) and patch or fix those pages first; confirm the vulnerable products in the inventory (AA26 31).

name: SoftEther masquerading as Windows binary
behaviour: SoftEther VPN renamed as a Windows process for persistence (the flagship walkthrough)
data_sources: Sysmon event 1 or EDR process telemetry: dest, process_name, process_path, original_file_name, parent_process_name
false_positives: Approved SoftEther installs (IT remote access); Software that legitimately ships its own conhost-named helper
positive_test: WS-0417: conhost.exe in C:\ProgramData\USOShared with original file name vpnbridge.exe fires once
negative_test: WS-0404's approved SoftEther VPN Client in Program Files and every real conhost.exe in System32 stay silent
response: Corroborate with AA26-D06 and AA26-D07 on the same host, check the owner's recent authentication, then request approval to isolate the host. Block the SoftEther dynamic DNS name and hunt the same hash across the fleet.

name: SoftEther dynamic DNS
behaviour: SoftEther reaching its server through dynamic DNS or VPN Azure
false_positives: Approved SoftEther users who rely on its dynamic DNS
positive_test: WS-0417 resolving vpn583920174.softether.net (18 lookups) fires once
negative_test: Hosts without SoftEther never resolve these names
response: Corroborate with AA26-D05 on the same host.

name: Autostart service outside system paths
behaviour: New auto-start service whose binary sits outside System32 and Program Files
data_sources: Windows System log event 7045: Computer, ServiceName, ImagePath, StartType
false_positives: Vendor updaters installed in ProgramData (for example the lab's Lenovo service)
positive_test: 'Console Host Service' running C:\ProgramData\USOShared\conhost.exe on WS-0417 fires
negative_test: The approved SoftEther client's service (Program Files) stays silent
response: Check the binary's original file name and signer; corroborate with process and network evidence.

name: EWS volume far above normal
behaviour: Scripted mailbox collection through Exchange Web Services (Curlc4.txt)
data_sources: Exchange IIS W3C logs: cs_username, c_ip, cs_uri_stem, cs_User_Agent, sc_status
false_positives: Mailbox migrations, eDiscovery exports, backup service accounts
positive_test: j.citizen: 2,400 EWS calls in one hour from 203.0.113.52 with no user agent (typical 3) fires once
negative_test: svc-crm's steady 160 calls an hour stays silent
response: Identify the client and source; if not a known integration, revoke the user's sessions and scope what was read.

name: Unapproved app reading many mailboxes
behaviour: office-cli style collection through a Microsoft 365 app registration
data_sources: Microsoft 365 unified audit log, MailItemsAccessed: AppId, MailboxOwnerUPN, ClientIPAddress
false_positives: A new approved integration not yet in the register
positive_test: The rogue app owned by j.citizen reading 7 mailboxes fires once
negative_test: The approved backup app reading every audited mailbox stays silent
response: Disable the app's credentials, review its consent and owner, and scope the mailboxes read.

name: New app secret or consent
behaviour: Credentials added to an application, or consent granted
data_sources: Microsoft 365 / Entra audit: UserId, Operation, ObjectId
false_positives: Routine secret rotation by the app owner
positive_test: j.citizen adding a secret to the rogue app the night before collection fires once
negative_test: Scheduled rotation by the integration team, with a change record, is closed as expected
response: Confirm with the app owner; if unexpected, remove the credential and review the app's permissions.

name: DCSync by non-machine account
behaviour: DCSync with DC.exe or secretsdump (directory replication by a non-DC account)
data_sources: Security event 4662 on domain controllers: SubjectUserName, Properties, AccessMask
false_positives: Microsoft Entra Connect (MSOL_ accounts); dcdiag and other replication tests
positive_test: Cannot be tested in the lab: no 4662 events, because the SACL was never set. Record it as a gap
negative_test: Domain controller computer accounts (ending in $) replicating normally stay silent
response: Treat every domain credential as exposed: contain the account, reset krbtgt twice, and plan eviction.

name: Advisory decoy file names
behaviour: Mail dumps and tools staged under the advisory's decoy names
data_sources: Sysmon event 11 or EDR file telemetry: dest, file_path, file_name
false_positives: Web deployments that legitimately ship Css.js or similar names
positive_test: The staged files on WS-0417 fire
negative_test: Ordinary image and script files with other names stay silent
response: Check the file's size, type and creator; a large 'image' or 'script' is likely an archive.

name: FishHub-style script stager
behaviour: FishHub phishing stager: a .vbe saved to %temp% and run by a script host
data_sources: Sysmon event 1 or EDR: dest, user, parent_process_name, process_name, process (command line)
false_positives: Rare: legacy logon scripts that use .vbe from temp folders
positive_test: Outlook > PowerShell > .vbe in %temp% > wscript on WS-0458 fires (2 rows)
negative_test: PowerShell without a .vbe in temp stays silent
response: Isolate the host with approval, block the stager domain, and check for collection and upload from the same host.

name: Known-bad domain resolved
behaviour: Resolution of an advisory or seizure domain (indicator matching)
false_positives: Security tools and sandboxes resolving indicators; Sinkholed domains after seizure
positive_test: WS-0458 resolving fym.linkedinns.net (DOJ seizure list, high confidence) fires once
negative_test: The j.citizen intrusion's new infrastructure matches nothing: the behavioural detections caught it
response: Confidence sets the response: high, investigate now; low, retro-hunt and corroborate before acting.

name: Connection to known-bad IP
behaviour: Traffic to an advisory or seizure IP address (indicator matching)
data_sources: Firewall or NetFlow: src, dest, bytes_out
false_positives: Shared hosting or cloud addresses that have been reassigned
positive_test: WS-0458 uploading 186 MB to 207.148.92.220 fires once (a low-confidence indicator that still matched)
negative_test: No other lab host touches the list
response: Corroborate with process and upload evidence on the host before containment.

name: Upload-heavy host
behaviour: Bulk upload from a host that normally downloads
data_sources: Firewall or NetFlow: src, bytes_in, bytes_out
positive_test: WS-0417 (5 hours through the tunnel) and WS-0458 (186 MB FishHub upload): 6 rows
negative_test: Workstations' normal download-heavy traffic stays silent
response: Score only; corroborate with the destination and the process responsible.

name: Integrity Tech behaviour chain
behaviour: Several AA26-281A behaviours on one identity or one host
data_sources: ES risk index (Risk data model): risk_object, risk_object_type, calculated_risk_score, ATT&CK tactic
false_positives: Shared or service identities that collect risk from many hosts
positive_test: j.citizen (identity) 200 across six tactics, and a.lim 100 across three: 2 findings
negative_test: WS-0417 (host, 80) and 203.0.113.47 (90) stay below 100 on their own
response: Follow 07-analyst-investigation-playbook.md: open the finding, read the contributing events, validate the identity, inspect the host, explain, escalate.
